name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,750

clue.text: One likely to go walking when out?

definitions.text: One likely to go walking when out?

blocks.clueFragment: One likely to go walking when out?
blocks.note: surface reading: a rambler who heads off on foot whenever they leave the house
setter's reading: 'out' means out cold, fast asleep, so this person walks while sleeping

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a hike and sets off on foot whenever they go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as outdoors, but it is the informal sense of unconscious or asleep. So we want a sleepwalker: SOMNAMBULIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker gets up and wanders about while deeply unconscious, which is what the Latin roots for sleep and walking describe.

clue.text: Obviously, I don't know if husband wears small wig

definitions.note: a gesture that says the words; the answer is the noun or verb for that gesture

indicators.note: whatever is worn sits on the outside, so the wearer ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
H is the abbreviation for husband
rug is slang for a toupee or wig

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark about whether a husband is wearing a little toupee.
explanation.walkthrough: The husband goes inside small wig, S + RUG, giving SHRUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is the everyday body-language way of saying you have no idea and couldn't care less.

clue.text: Old foreign coin female pal reminted

indicators.note: a coin reminted is melted down and struck again in a new form, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's friend has an old foreign coin melted down and struck afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The minting indicator fits the coin theme neatly, hiding that it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian Maple Leaf is a bullion coin issued by Canada's mint, so a foreign coin to a British solver.

clue.text: A couple of lines I will snort right quickly

definitions.note: a musical tempo direction, used as an adverb

indicators.note: to snort something is to draw it inside through the nose, so one piece takes another in

blocks.note: taken as written
L is line, so two lines are LL
the ego is the self, the 'I'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone takes a couple of lines of cocaine and snorts them fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' and 'snort' suggest drugs, but the lines are just letters and snorting means taking in. Allegro is Italian for lively and marks a fast tempo in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the Italian tempo marking telling performers to play at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: In hearing, pay off flappers one after the other

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read, so the spelling of the words spoken may differ

blocks.note: to pay someone off is to buy them off, to bribe
terns are seabirds, things that flap their wings

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to hear about paying off 1920s flapper girls in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flappers' suggests the fashionable young women of the 1920s, but here they are birds, terns. BUY TERNS said out loud gives BY TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things by turns means alternating, each taking their go in sequence rather than together.

clue.text: Rabies is found in silly-billy's saliva

indicators.note: something found inside other words is lying within their run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A medical fact: rabies is carried in the saliva, even that of a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans billY'S SAliva. It is apt, since rabies really is passed on through saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyssa is the medical and zoological term for rabies, from the Greek for madness or frenzy.

clue.text: Dad uses IQ to thrash enlisted soldiers

indicators.note: a thrashing gives a real beating, knocking the letters into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father relies on his superior intelligence to beat a group of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses' reads as a verb in the surface but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaddie is British informal slang for a private or ordinary soldier of the lowest rank.

clue.text: French trio who play with each other for fun?

definitions.text: French trio who play with each other for fun?

blocks.clueFragment: French trio who play with each other for fun?
blocks.note: surface reading: three French musicians who play music together for pleasure
setter's reading: the play is sexual, a three-way domestic arrangement

explanation.surface: Three amateur French musicians who get together to play for the love of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trio' and 'play' suggest chamber music; the play is of a more intimate kind, and the phrase for it is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means a household of three, now used for a sexual relationship among three people living together.

clue.text: Group of cops backtracking in dock over regret

indicators.note: going back along the track one came by means running the other way

blocks.note: to dock a tail is to lop it
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Police officers in the dock backtrack on their evidence, full of regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a courtroom, but it is the verb meaning cut short. LOP, O and RUE run backwards give EUROPOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Europol is the European Union's law enforcement agency, coordinating police forces across member states.

clue.text: Problem in centre of Saint-Denis covered in paper?

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the letters at the heart of the word are kept
one thing placed in another sits enclosed by it

blocks.note: the two middle letters of this ten-letter name
an issue is a problem

explanation.surface: A problem in the heart of a Paris suburb gets papered over.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint-Denis is a suburb of Paris, and its ten letters give an even-sized centre of two. The question mark flags a slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, so something tissued has been wrapped or covered in that material.

clue.text: A few days away for relations?

definitions.text: A few days away for relations?

blocks.clueFragment: A few days away for relations?
blocks.note: surface reading: a short trip to visit family members
setter's reading: sexual relations, the purpose of a short illicit getaway

explanation.surface: A short trip away to see the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' reads as relatives, but it means sexual relations. The answer is British slang for a romantic, often secret, weekend away.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a short trip taken by a couple, often illicitly, mainly for sex.

clue.text: Side that can come with fish

blocks.note: first meaning: a point of view or aspect of a story
second meaning: to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A side dish, like chips, that can be served with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a side order with a fish supper; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a particular viewpoint on an issue, and to angle is to go fishing with hook and line.

clue.text: Euro-MP regularly has quick look around plant

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
going around something means surrounding it on all sides

blocks.note: to have a gander is British slang for a quick look
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A member of the European Parliament often glances around an industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory tour, but it is a botanical plant. Gander is British slang in the phrase 'have a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herbaceous shrub of the mint family, genus Teucrium, grown in gardens and hedges.

clue.text: Avoid answering Bill if the First Lady’s about

indicators.note: being about something means being all round it

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
a bill is a poster, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A politician dodges questions about Bill when the President's wife is around.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest Bill and Hillary Clinton, but the First Lady is Eve, the first woman, and a bill is an AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade a question is to dodge it, sidestepping without giving a straight reply.

clue.text: City abroad made smart after rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the material together again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign city was smartened up after a regeneration project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made smart' reads as a phrase meaning smartened; its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, so a foreign city to a British setter.

clue.text: Four-letter word upset nicest boy

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swearing has shocked the most well-behaved boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' is a nine-letter definition; the phrase is the idiom for a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-letter word is the idiom for a swear word, since many common English expletives have four letters.

clue.text: Pregnant old flame exercises court worker

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
PE is physical education, school exercises
CT is the abbreviation for court
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A pregnant former lover works out, and a court worker is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court worker' looks like one person, an usher or clerk, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is one awaiting the birth of her baby, a common euphemism for being with child.

clue.text: Military group foes track all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered in every direction, out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military unit follows its enemies wherever they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' reads as a verb for pursuing the enemy; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a unit of armed forces assembled for a specific operation or mission.

clue.text: Singer smuggling international males' old gear

indicators.note: smuggled goods are hidden inside something else, so one piece is carried within another

blocks.note: one who sings to the police is an informer, a rat
I is the abbreviation for international
males are men

explanation.surface: A singer smuggles men's clothing across borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist but is a grass who sings to the police. 'Old' tells you the answer is an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic or literary word for clothing, and gear is informal for clothes.

clue.text: Similar to a looker I picked up and fancy

indicators.note: to pick something up is to catch it by ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: the pronoun and the organ of sight share one sound
to fancy is to like

explanation.surface: Someone says they caught the eye of an attractive person and fancy them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker' suggests an attractive person, but it is literally the thing you look with.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling an eye in shape or appearance; an eye is the organ of vision, hence a looker.

clue.text: Outdated sexual advance ending in trouble

indicators.note: the ending is the final part, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: to make a pass is to make a sexual advance
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned come-on ends up causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word is written with an accent, which crosswords drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word describes something no longer fashionable, past its prime and out of date.

clue.text: Put too much chilli in stuffing I serve cop

indicators.note: stuffing things in crams them in any old how, messing up their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook admits to overdoing the chilli in the stuffing they serve a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like the food being served; it is the signal to rearrange the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli is a spice, so adding far too much of it is seasoning a dish excessively.

clue.text: Secret police making one finally unearth cache

indicators.note: to make one thing into another is to swap it for something new
finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the Stasi was East Germany's secret police
the Roman numeral for one, which is swapped out
the final letter, which replaces the numeral

explanation.surface: Secret police force someone to dig up a hidden hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the I of STASI (one) into the last letter of unearth, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or valuables, and a stash is the informal word for one.

clue.text: Conservative leader? Disgusting oddball!

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
rank means foul or disgusting

explanation.surface: A scornful verdict on the leader of the Conservative Party as a revolting weirdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative leader' reads as the party boss but gives only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an eccentric person with odd fixed ideas, much like an oddball or weirdo.

clue.text: Beer around four makes you full of life

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A beer at about four o'clock perks you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around four' reads as a time of day, but 'four' is a Roman numeral and 'around' wraps the beer about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively, animated and vigorous is being alive in the figurative sense of bursting with energy.

clue.text: Blue item of luggage one thought pretty pathetic

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a suitcase is an item of luggage

explanation.surface: Someone thought a blue suitcase looked rather pitiful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'one thought' as someone's opinion; it is the definition's way of describing a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sad case is a colloquial term for a person regarded as pitiable, inadequate or socially hopeless.

clue.text: I oversaw The Scotsman and another national

blocks.note: taken as written
to run something is to oversee it
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor boasts of running The Scotsman and another national paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is an Edinburgh newspaper and a 'national' sounds like another paper, but here the Scotsman is just a man called IAN, and the national is a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a particular country, and an Iranian is a citizen of Iran.

clue.text: A politician assassinated by US cops on roofless house

blocks.note: taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament
a hit is a contract killing
the heat is American slang for the police
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A politician was murdered by American police in a house with no roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roofless house' seems to be where the killing happened; it is the definition, as a house is a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a theatre auditorium, and an amphitheatre is an open-air arena with tiered seating and no covering.
